chose: One strike family for the study nudge's browsers and the Jobs notice's phones, built once in file_host::strikes. (1) Storage: columns strikes, set_aside_at, set_aside_why and last_probe_at on push_subscriptions and jobs_notice_device, not a shared table. (2) Per-sender closed strike sets, where a strike is only the device's own failure: web push strikes on a delivery timeout or no answer, never on 400 (our payload or VAPID JWT), 403 (our key), 413, 429, 5xx or a send never made; FCM strikes on 403 SENDER_ID_MISMATCH, and on a 400 only when another phone took the same notice in that pass, never on 401, the token endpoint, an unsigned JWT, 429, 5xx or no answer, so a lone phone's 400 never strikes. (3) A set-aside device is included at most once a day, only in a send that happens anyway: accepting brings it back (strikes = 0), failing leaves it aside with no new strike or count, and registering again also brings it back. Setting one aside is counted once (study-nudge/device_set_aside, jobs-notice/phone_set_aside). A device is set aside after 3 strikes in a row: the owner said 'a few timeouts' on server#1180, and 3 is the coordinator's reading of 'a few', part of this call. That a delivery accepted later brings a device back is the owner's own rule.
options: Columns on each device table, per-sender closed strike sets, and a once-a-day inclusion only within real sends
A shared device_strikes table keyed by endpoint or token, which holds an endpoint or a token a second time (docs/identity.md)
Forget a phone on FCM error codes as UNREGISTERED does: a payload bug of ours reads as INVALID_ARGUMENT and would forget every phone (ruled out on server#1222)
Re-registration as the only way back, so the owner's 'a delivery it accepts later brings it back' could never happen, since a set-aside device is never sent to
A scheduled probe, which is a clock (docs/home-compute.md)
gray: Whether a failure is the device's or home's can't always be told: a lone phone's FCM 400 may be its token or our notice, so it never strikes, and server#1222 stays open for a single-phone owner except on SENDER_ID_MISMATCH. And a record no phone is sent to (every phone set aside) is owed to none, so it is not counted lost each morning: setting each phone aside was the count. The owner's words cover timeouts only. Striking on a device's own refusals (FCM SENDER_ID_MISMATCH, a 400 beside a phone that took the notice) and on web push's no answer is the coordinator's reading on server#1222, not the owner's.

Devices are then sent to every time again.
